whenToUse: You delete items that are often removed and restored, such as emails, tasks, or files.
Asking for confirmation every time would slow down repeated work.
It's fine to delay applying the change on the server by a few seconds.
whenNotToUse: The action can't be undone, such as a payment or deleting an account (use a confirmation dialog).
The action notifies someone else right away (it can't be taken back once sent).
Several steps are tangled together, making it hard to restore the exact state.

alternatives.name: Confirmation Dialog
alternatives.reason: Asking once more before something irreversible.

alternatives.name: Toast
alternatives.reason: Briefly reporting a result that doesn't need undoing.

accessibility: The snackbar has role="status", so it reads the result without moving focus.
Hovering or focusing it stops the timer, so it doesn't disappear before people reach the undo button (WCAG 2.2.1).
The time-left line is decorative, so it's aria-hidden and hidden with reduced motion.
Allow undoing only one action at a time; a new action commits the previous one at once.
